entries.title: R.D. 28 aprile 1938, n. 1165: Approvazione del testo unico delle disposizioni sull'edilizia popolare ed economica (Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 177, 5 agosto 1938, supplemento ordinario)
text: The consolidated law on public housing of 1938, the general frame for the provincial housing institutes. It knows no “semirurale” category: “rural” appears only in a tax exemption and in one clause on bodies building “borgate rurali”. This research reads it as the legal vehicle of the Semirurali all the same, with ministerial subsidies on top.
The scan's two-column text is scrambled, and whether that clause stood in the 1938 original could not be confirmed.
facts: Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 177, 5 Aug. 1938, ordinary supplement, carrying R.D. 28 Apr. 1938, n. 1165, the T.U. on public and economic housing (manifest).

The general frame for the IFACPs: constitution and recognition, mortgages and state contributions, Ministry of Public Works oversight; art. 27: the president of each provincial institute "è nominato con decreto Reale su proposta del Ministro pei lavori pubblici" (notes 01, §1–2, [V]).

No "semirurale" category: "rural" appears only in the tax exemption for "fabbricati rurali" (art. 164) and in art. 16 n. 12° on bodies "che provvedano alla costruzione di borgate rurali" (notes 01, §2, [V]).
The OCR is scrambled by the two-column layout, so whether art. 16 n. 12° was in the 1938 original could not be confirmed (manifest; notes 01, §2).
The notes read it as the legal vehicle of the semirurale type, with ministerial subsidies (notes 01, §2, [INF]).
entries.rights: An official act. Not protected by copyright (L. 633/1941, art. 5).

confidence.note: The OCR is scrambled; whether art. 16 n. 12° stood in the 1938 original is not confirmed.

entries.title: Turris Babel, no. 1, March 1985: Semirurali – prima parte
text: The first of three issues of the architects' journal Turris Babel on the Semirurali, with Carlo Azzolini's account of the 1930s and facsimiles of the housing institute's drawings. The general plan at 1:1000 is signed “Ing. Giulio Garbini”. Its streets are named after Italian cities and meet at a Piazza Pontinia, a name taken from the reclaimed marshes south of Rome.
The elevations show two-storey houses with pitched roofs and outside stairs. Plots were cut at 600 square metres for four dwellings. The pictures here are crops from the scan.
facts: Turris Babel no. 1, March 1985, with Carlo Azzolini, "Semirurali – prima parte", pp. 7–34, on the 1930s, and facsimiles of the IFACP site plan, type elevations, plans and sections; the scan has no text layer (manifest).

The site plan "PLANIMETRIA GENERALE – CASE SEMIRURALI – BOLZANO – SCALA 1:1000" is signed "Ing. Giulio Garbini"; its streets are named after Italian cities, around PIAZZA PONTINIA (notes 01, §1, §3, [V]); the square's name is Agro Pontino toponymy (notes 01, §5, [S]).
Azzolini: the institute was founded on 10 April 1934 to house the workforce of the new industrial zone; Garbini cut the plots at "600 mq per 4 alloggi" (notes 01, §1, §3, [S]).

Seen in the image (p. 25, fig. 40): a grid of small house plots between VIA MILANO and the river ISARCO, PIAZZA PONTINIA at the west end, two north arrows, the legend "I° LOTTO / II° / III° / LAVATOI" and a handwritten signature at lower right.

Seen in the image (p. 27, figs. 42–45): elevations "PROSPETTI SCALA 1:100" of two-storey houses with pitched roofs and external stairs, a handwritten signature under figs. 44 and 45, and text quoting the comparison with "la piccola casa di Predappio".
Seen in the image (p. 28, figs. 46–49): four symmetrical ground-floor plans drawn in heavy black walls, beside text on the first lot of 340 dwellings inaugurated on 8 October 1939.

Seen in the image (p. 31, figs. 60–70): two sections, one marked "SEZIONE A-B SCALA 1:50", and nine 1939 photographs of finished houses with fenced gardens, people digging a vegetable plot and a shop signed "SPACCIO COOPERATIVO N 37".
Seen in the image (fig. 61, detail): a round stamp, "IL DIRETTORE TECNICO", the signature "Ing. Giulio Garbini" and "BOLZANO FEB…" with the year unclear.

entries.title: Turris Babel, no. 2, June 1985: Semirurali – seconda parte
text: The second issue, on the redevelopment of 1976–83 that replaced the Semirurali: commissions to Aymonino and to Darbourne & Darke, and in December 1983 a cut in density “da 5,0 a 3,5 mc/mq”. Its interviews are a lead for the biography of Garbini.
facts: Turris Babel no. 2, June 1985: F. Bortolotti, G. Plaickner and F. Anesi, "Semirurali – seconda parte", on the redevelopment of 1976–83; the scan has no text layer (manifest).

Lot chronology: Oct. 1978 Aymonino commissioned for lot 1; Nov. 1978 competition for lot 2, won by Darbourne & Darke in Apr. 1981; Mar. 1982 lot 3 to Darbourne & Darke, Abram & Schnabl and Planungsgruppe Meran (notes 01, §6, [S]).
Dec. 1983: the Piano di Attuazione is modified, density cut "da 5,0 a 3,5 mc/mq" (notes 01, §6, [S]).
One of three primary-rich Turris Babel issues on the Semirurali; its interviews are named as a lead for Garbini's biography (notes 01, §1, §6).

entries.title: Turris Babel, no. 15, December 1988: Semirurali III
text: The third issue. The housing institute looks back on a quarter built “con gli evidenti riferimenti della ‘città giardino’” to ease “il problema psicologico dell'inurbamento di popolazioni rurali chiamate specialmente dalle provincie venete”. The redevelopment plan of 1976–78 foresaw “ca. 2.000 alloggi in sostituzione degli attuali 800”.
Its bibliography corrects a date: the Italian daily's series on the workers' city ran in autumn 1937, not in 1936.
facts: Turris Babel no. 15, Dec. 1988, "Semirurali III": the IPEAA account "Le Semirurali dell'Istituto", the fourth-lot competition and a "Repertorio bibliografico"; it has an OCR text layer (manifest).

The IPEAA looks back on a quarter built "con gli evidenti riferimenti della 'città giardino'" for "il problema psicologico dell'inurbamento di popolazioni rurali chiamate specialmente dalle provincie venete" (notes 01, §3, [S]).
The 1976–78 Piano di Attuazione: "ca. 2.000 alloggi in sostituzione degli attuali 800", about 250 billion lire (notes 01, §6, [S]).
The Repertorio dates LPB's "Le case per il Popolo. Crescita della città operaia" to autumn 1937, against the "1936" given in the secondary literature (notes 01, §3, [S]).

A German-language article, probably Plaickner's, quotes Franz Seldte on the small settlement as "die beste Form der Arbeiterwohnstätte": a 1980s editorial comparison, not a period Bolzano source (notes 01, §5, [S]).
1981 census for Don Bosco: 2,402 of 4,855 occupied dwellings public; 1,112 German-speakers; the OCR layout leaves the attribution of these notes uncertain (notes 01, §5–6, [S]).
